reason: पुमासं is no form of पुंस्; the accusative is पुमांसम्, so the anusvāra was dropped.
पत्त्रिन् is a valid spelling (MW headword pattrin) and the book uses the same त्त्र in पतत्त्रिन् (1.14.34, 36) and तोत्त्र, so it is the edition's spelling, not a slip.
अङ्गलीयक is no word; the ring is अङ्गुलीयक and the ु sign is missing in print.
The print has the correct मुक्तपुष्पावकीर्णेन (ी on क, reph and े on र्णे); the stray े exists only in our text layer.
The verse names the elephant classes भद्र, मन्द्र, मृग and their mixtures (भद्रमन्द्र… in the same verse), so मद्रैः lacks the न्.

The king himself watches the subjects through spies (the edition's own translation: "seeing everything with his eyes in the form of spies"), which needs the active अवेक्षमाणः, the form the book uses some fifteen times; the passive participle cannot govern this sense.
The print has छ्र without ु, which gives the non-word एतच्छ्रत्वा for एतच्छ्रुत्वा.
राजन् + ऋषि gives राजर्षि; राजार्षि is not a word.
Viśvāmitra's patronymic is कौशिक, spelt so everywhere else in the book; कौसिक occurs only here.
ववनम् is no word; the formula is इदं वचनमब्रवीत्.
The weapon's name is from नैराश्य (MW), which the book spells with श everywhere else; नैरास्य is a misspelling.
With vocative राघवौ and युवाम् the verb must be second-person dual रक्षतम्; रक्षताम् is third person.
प्राहसन्नित्यं is valid sandhi of the singular imperfect प्राहसत् + नित्यम्, and the edition's translation ("laughed to see them drowning") reads a finite verb, so nothing is wrong.
यज्ञहनः (genitive or plural of यज्ञहन्) cannot stand as predicate of अयं; यज्ञहरः "stealer of our sacrifice" fits, and र/न is a one-letter slip.
The pāda सुपर्णमनिलोपम् has only 7 syllables and अनिलोपम् is no form; the accusative is अनिलोपमम्.
The print's ligature is the same ह्रु glyph as in व्याजह्रुः (3.52.34), but the sage is जह्नु, as the book prints in verses 35 and 38 of this sarga.
द्रंष्ट्र is no word; the fang is दंष्ट्रा, so the र stroke under द is extra.
The royal tent is the feminine उपकार्या (MW; the book has उपकार्याः at 1.13.9 and in the Uttara), so the accusative is उपकार्याम्.
जामदग्नय is no word and makes the pāda 9 syllables; the patronymic is जामदग्न्यः.
सदिता is no word; the sense is भर्तृभिः सहिताः "together with their husbands", so द is a slip for ह.
Sītā "had been brought" needs the causative participle आनायिता; the agent noun आनयिता gives no sense.
अभ्यसूय्य is the regular absolutive of the denominative असूय with a preverb (असूय + ल्यप्, final a dropped by अतो लोपः, giving -असूय्य), so the printed form is correct.
यौवराज्ये भरतं has only 7 syllables; the च of the other editions restores the 8-syllable pāda.
प्रत्युदीक्षेया is no form; with मा स्म the second-person optative middle is प्रत्युदीक्षेथाः, written -था before मा.
Kaikeyī speaks of herself as मां … गताम् इतः "me gone hence"; the nominative गता cannot agree with मां, so भ is a slip for म.
पितरपेक्षया is no possible form; the genitive पितुः keeps the 8 syllables of the pāda and gives "out of regard for your father".
The infinitive of प्र-√स्था is प्रस्थातुम्; प्रस्थितुम् is impossible.
The subject (Rāma, धर्मात्मा) is singular, so वयसा च अमरप्रभः → चामरप्रभः; the plural ending is an extra ा.
अनालम्भ is no word (आलम्भ is "seizing, killing"); "without support" is अनालम्ब (MW), a ब/भ slip.
समक्षसे is no verb form; the ी of समीक्षसे is missing.
वि + अतीत gives व्यतीत; व्यातीता has an extra ा and is no form.
With object रामं the sense "having banished Rāma" needs the causative absolutive प्रव्राज्य, which the book prints in the same phrase at 2.79.2; प्रव्रज्य "having gone forth" cannot take an object.
उपैष्यथः is a correct second-person dual, and the epic construes भवत् with second-person verbs (the book has स भवान् … कर्तुमर्हसि at 3.40.16), so the reading is valid.
Before इव the noun must be करेणवः → करेणव इव "like she-elephants"; करेणेव would double the इव.
The messengers are the ones beholding Viṣṇu's footprint (the edition's translation: "beholding"), which needs the active प्रेक्षमाणाः, the book's usual form; the passive participle is an extra य्.
The print really has निषष्ण्णं, with a doubled ष; the participle is निषण्ण.
Rubbing salt into a wound is आ-√धा "put" (आदधाः); आददाः "you took" gives the wrong sense, a द/ध slip.
Doubling a consonant after reph is a valid spelling, and the book spells this word with र्द्ध again in समरगर्द्धिना (7.14.2) and महर्द्धिनां (5.8.5), so it is the edition's orthography, not an error.
Pastes are kept in caskets (समुद्ग), not oceans; र is a slip for ग.
अब्रतीत् is no word; the verb is अब्रवीत्.
अभिषिञ्चन is no noun (not in MW or Apte); the noun is अभिषेचन, and the edition's translation reads "by getting yourself consecrated".
The feminine accusative उचिताम् agrees with nothing; "what fitting and dear thing shall I do" needs neuter उचितम् with प्रियं … किम्.
त्रैलोक्य is neuter, so the accusative is त्रैलोक्यम्; त्रैलोक्याम् has an extra ा.
Chariots on rough ground and ministers who share the king's fate "are broken", भज्यन्ते (√भञ्ज्); भुज्यन्ते gives no sense.
The imperfect of प्र + causative √शुभ् needs the augment, प्राशोभयत, and the edition translates "adorned"; a dropped ा.
The trees are "struck" by portent-winds, अभिहताः; अभिरताः "delighting in" gives no sense, a र/ह slip.
The nominative construes with पापः, and the edition's own translation reads it so ("although a tremor ran through his limbs"), so -वेपथुः is a deliberate reading of this edition.
The pronoun is युष्माकम्, with retroflex ष; युस्माकं is a non-word.
कृत्कृत्य is no word and leaves the pāda at 7 syllables; कृतकृत्य mends both.
The two breasts are the subject, so the verb is the dual न अभिभातः "do not shine" (11 syllables kept); नाभिपातः has no construction, a भ/प slip.
दिधक्ष्यामि is no form (desiderative future would be दिधक्षिष्यामि, the plain future धक्ष्यामि); the present desiderative दिधक्षामि keeps the 8 syllables and the sense "I wish to burn".
The distance is the क्रोश (the edition's translation: "a distance of two leagues"); कोश has no such sense, so the र is dropped.
√लभ् takes no nasal in the imperfect, so समालम्भत is no form; "she clung to Lakṣmaṇa" is सम्-आ-√लम्ब्, समालम्बत.
अच्छिन्दन्ताम् is no dual form; the epic thematic dual imperfect is अच्छिन्दताम्, with the same 8 syllables.
The print has सुग्रीवचनात् with one व; सुग्रीववचनात् restores the word and the 8-syllable pāda.
विकान्त is no word; the र of विक्रान्त "valiant" is missing.
जम्मुः is no form; the perfect of √गम् is जग्मुः.
बाह्व्यो is no word; the feminine plural of बहु is बह्व्यः, a minimal fix that drops the extra ा.
वसुधायं is no form; the locative "on the ground" is वसुधायाम्.
The subject is the eight monkeys named in verse 35, so the verb must be plural अभ्यषिञ्चन्त; the singular drops न्.
The rivers hasten to the ocean, द्रुतम् "swiftly"; दृत is only a rare lexicon word and gives no sense here, the common ृ/्रु slip.
सु + अवेक्षित gives स्ववेक्षितम् "well considered" (the edition's translation: "well thought out"); स्ववीक्षितं is broken sandhi.
The participle of √ब्रू is ब्रुवाण with short ु.
बहुसास्र is no word and leaves the pāda at 7 syllables; बहुसाहस्रैः restores both.
अभिध्नन् is no form; the participle of अभि-√हन् is अभिघ्नन् ("smashing with his breast"), a ध/घ slip.
विलोकयत् is neither a participle nor an augmented imperfect; the verse continues ददर्श of verse 204, so विलोकयन् is needed, a त/न slip.
Feminine दंष्ट्राभिः cannot agree with masculine बहुभिः शूरैः राक्षसैः; the edition's translation ("ogres distinguished by tusks") needs दंष्ट्रिभिः.
The compound qualifies instrumental रथैः like the other adjectives, so it ends in -ऐः; the feminine accusative -ईः agrees with nothing.
बिभूषित is no word; the book prints विभूषित everywhere else.
The faces have closed teeth, दन्त (the edition's translation: "teeth concealed"); दान्त "tamed / of ivory" makes no sense.

परिविद्ध्य is no absolutive (that of परि-√व्यध् is परिविध्य, which also gives no sense with a drum); the edition's translation "pressing a wooden tomtom to her bosom" and the other editions need परिपीड्य.

अपारवार is a meaningful compound, "without limit (पार) or bound in time (वार)", and the edition's translation reads exactly "limitless in time or space", so it is the edition's reading, not a प/व slip.
कंचित् त्राणम् construes as "anyone as a refuge" (masculine pronoun with a predicative neuter noun), and the edition translates "finding no saviour", so the printed reading is valid.
आनाय is only a noun ("net"); the gerund "taking away his merit" is आदाय (the edition's translation: "takes away all his merit").

The print shows a space between गल्मे and बहभिः that our text lacks, and the marks below the line are missing or cut off at the page edge; अस्थापयद् गुल्मे बहुभिः restores the words, the sense and the 16 syllables.
विचिन्विता is no form; the instrumental of विचिन्वत् agreeing with अधनेन is विचिन्वता.
The Vāruṇa weapon was "rendered ineffectual" (the edition's translation), विहतम्; विहितम् "arranged" gives no sense.
